### workspace step --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace step done [--status pass|fail|done|running|needs_input|stuck] [--step STEP] [--summary TEXT] [--code WORD] [--run RUN_ID] [--json]
       workspace step status [--run RUN_ID] [--json]
       workspace step expect-fail [--match-file PATH] [--timeout SECONDS] [--] FILE...
       workspace step check-ids --prefix P[,P...] --defined FILE (--covered FILE [--each-line-matches REGEX] | --plan-details [--name WORKSPACE]) [--allow-missing] [--json]

done and status are for the agent working on a workflow step, run from the pane the run
is bound to. Neither is required: a step is decided when the agent's turn ends, from the
files it was told to leave and the step's check (see `workspace workflow --help`).
expect-fail is run by a step's `require: exec:` proof, from no pane: it checks that the
given tests fail before the fix. check-ids checks that every numbered ID one file
defines (R1, AC-3) is named by another file or by the plan's Task details.

  done         Record what you say about a workflow step, then end your turn
  status       Show which workflow run, step and attempt this pane is on
  expect-fail  Check that the given tests fail (a fail-first proof)
  check-ids    Check that every numbered ID one file defines is covered (a coverage check)
Run `workspace step VERB --help` for a verb's options.

        --status STATUS              done: pass (default), fail, or a stated status: done, running, needs_input, stuck
        --step STEP                  done: the fan_out sibling to report on, when this pane is bound to its group
        --summary TEXT               done: one line about what was done, or what is left
        --code WORD                  done: a word for why, kept with a failed step: starts with a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, _ (at most 40); not one the engine uses (e.g. check_failed, head_moved)
        --run RUN_ID                 done, status: the run to work on when this process has no pane binding (a subagent or background run, no $TMUX_PANE); with no --run, the checkout's one going run is used when unambiguous
        --match-file PATH            expect-fail: a file whose text (trimmed) the failing tests' output must hold
        --timeout SECONDS            expect-fail: seconds the tests may run (default 240)
        --prefix P                   check-ids: letters an ID starts with, such as R or AC (repeatable, or comma-separated)
        --defined FILE               check-ids: the file whose lines start with the IDs
        --covered FILE               check-ids: the file that must name every ID
        --plan-details               check-ids: the workspace plan's ## Task details must name every ID, instead of --covered
        --each-line-matches REGEX    check-ids: an ID counts as covered only on a line of --covered that matches
        --allow-missing              check-ids: pass when the --defined file does not exist
        --name WORKSPACE             check-ids: the workspace whose plan --plan-details reads (default: the current one)
        --json                       done, status, check-ids: print one JSON document (see docs/README.workflow.md)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace step status    # which run, step and attempt this pane is on
  workspace step done --summary "Plan written; three commits."    # record a pass, then end your turn
  workspace step done --status fail --summary "Two specs still fail in billing."    # fail the step at the turn's end
  workspace step done --status fail --code not_reproduced --summary "The failure did not happen locally."    # fail it with a word for why
  workspace step expect-fail --match-file .workflow/RUN/failure.txt -- spec/models/invoice_spec.rb    # exits 0 only when the test fails with that text
  workspace step check-ids --prefix R --defined requirements.md --covered plan.md    # exits 0 only when plan.md names every R
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace step done --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace step done [--status pass|fail|done|running|needs_input|stuck] [--step STEP] [--summary TEXT] [--code WORD] [--run RUN_ID] [--json]

Record what you say about a workflow step, then end your turn.

For the agent working on a workflow step, run from the pane the run is bound to. --status fail fails
the step at the turn's end without running its check. It is not required: a step is decided when the
agent's turn ends, from the files it was told to leave and the step's check (see `workspace
workflow --help`).

Options:
    --status STATUS              pass (default), fail, or a stated status: done, running, needs_input, stuck (--summary is its detail)
    --step STEP                  The fan_out sibling to report on, when this pane is bound to its group
    --summary TEXT               One line about what was done, or what is left
    --code WORD                  A word for why, kept with a failed step: starts with a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, _ (at most 40); not one the engine uses (e.g. check_failed, head_moved)
    --run RUN_ID                 The run to report on, when this process has no pane binding (a subagent or background run, no $TMUX_PANE); with no --run, the checkout's one going run is used when unambiguous
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace step done    # record a pass for the step your pane is on; then end your turn
  workspace step done --summary "Plan written; three commits."    # record a pass with one line on what was done
  workspace step done --status fail --summary "Two specs still fail in billing."    # fail the step when the turn ends, without running its check
  workspace step done --status fail --code not_reproduced --summary "The failure did not happen locally."    # fail it with a word for why, kept with the failed step
  workspace step done --summary "Docs written" --json    # the same as one JSON document; outside a run's pane it exits 1 with not_bound
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace step status --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace step status [--run RUN_ID] [--json]

Show which workflow run, step and attempt this pane is on.

Also shows where the step's instructions are, and whether the files the step must leave are there: written this attempt, non-empty, regular files and not links (problem names the rule broken). Run
from the pane the run is bound to. With no pane binding (no $TMUX_PANE), the checkout's one going run is used when unambiguous; name it with --run.

Options:
    --run RUN_ID                 The run to read, when this process has no pane binding (a subagent or background run, no $TMUX_PANE); with no --run, the checkout's one going run is used when unambiguous
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace step status    # which workflow run, step and attempt this pane is on, and the files the step must leave
  workspace step status --json    # the same as one JSON document, with whether each file is there (produces); outside a run's pane it exits 1 with not_bound
  workspace step status --json | jq '.step.produces'    # list the files the step must leave, and whether each was written this attempt (current)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace step expect-fail --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace step expect-fail [--match-file PATH] [--timeout SECONDS] [--] FILE...

Check that the given tests fail (a fail-first proof).

Run by a step's `require: exec:` proof, from no pane: it finds the workspace from the directory it runs
in (the checkout) and never reads TMUX_PANE or a pane binding. Runs the workspace's commands.test with the
FILEs appended (shell-escaped) through `sh -c` in its own process group, prints the tests' output, then one
line starting `expect-fail:` (only the last 1 MB of output is printed, with a line saying when it was cut).
Exits 0 only when the tests fail and, with --match-file, their stdout and stderr together hold the file's
text (trimmed) as one exact substring. Exits 1 when no FILE is given, commands.test is unset, the match file
is missing, a link, empty or over 4096 bytes, the tests pass, the text is missing, or the tests run past
--timeout.
commands.test must take test files as arguments. It does not prove the tests fail for the right reason.

Options:
    --match-file PATH            A file (at most 4096 bytes, not a link) whose text, trimmed, the failing tests' output must hold as one exact substring; relative to the working directory
    --timeout SECONDS            Seconds the tests may run before they are stopped (default 240)
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace step expect-fail -- spec/models/invoice_spec.rb    # exits 0 only when the test fails
  workspace step expect-fail --match-file .workflow/RUN/failure.txt -- spec/models/invoice_spec.rb    # exits 0 only when it fails with the text of failure.txt
  workspace step expect-fail --match-file {{artifacts}}/failure.txt --timeout 840 -- {{changed.tests}}    # the exec: line of a fail-first proof (with timeout: 15m on the entry)
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace step check-ids --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace step check-ids --prefix P[,P...] --defined FILE (--covered FILE [--each-line-matches REGEX] | --plan-details [--name WORKSPACE]) [--allow-missing] [--json]

Check that every numbered ID one file defines is covered (a coverage check).

Reads the IDs at the start of a line of --defined: a prefix, an optional `-`, then digits (R1, AC-3). AC-3 and
AC3 are the same ID; R1 is not R10 or R1a. Each must be named, anywhere, by the --covered file, or
by the `## Task details` section of the workspace's plan with --plan-details (the plan must exist and have
tasks). Relative files resolve against $WORKSPACE_RUN_ARTIFACTS when it is set and not empty, else the
working directory. Files must be regular files (not links) of at most 1 MiB. No IDs defined passes.
Prints one line (stdout when covered, stderr otherwise), or with --json one document on stdout; read --json's
reason, not the line. The line starts `check-ids:`, except that uncovered IDs with --plan-details print
`In no task of ## Task details: R2 R3`, as the rpiv presets always have. Exits 0 when every ID is covered, 1 when one is not or the check can't run (missing plan, missing
--defined without --allow-missing, missing or unreadable --covered, a line that matches too slowly). A usage
error (a bad or missing flag, an invalid regex) exits 1 with code usage, as for any command.

Options:
    --prefix P                   Letters an ID starts with, such as R or AC; repeat the flag or separate with commas
    --defined FILE               The file whose lines start with the IDs
    --covered FILE               The file that must name every ID (with --each-line-matches, on a matching line)
    --plan-details               Use the plan's `## Task details` section instead of --covered
    --each-line-matches REGEX    With --covered: an ID counts as covered only on a line that names it and matches REGEX (1 second limit per line)
    --allow-missing              Pass when the --defined file does not exist
    --name WORKSPACE             With --plan-details: the workspace whose plan to read (default: the current one; not_in_workspace outside any)
    --json                       Print {schema_version, ok, prefixes, defined, covered, missing, reason, defined_path, covered_path}; reason is null, uncovered, no_plan, defined_absent, covered_absent or regex_timeout
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace step check-ids --prefix R --defined requirements.md --plan-details --allow-missing    # the plan check: every R of requirements.md is in a task's details
  workspace step check-ids --prefix AC --defined spec.md --covered report.md --each-line-matches PASS    # every AC-n has a PASS line in the report
  workspace step check-ids --prefix R,AC --defined spec.md --covered plan.md --json    # the same as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end
